Founder.title: Three founders,
intro: Sura Essence began with a shared frustration and a shared hope. Too many visitors arrive in Rwanda and spend their first days stitching together drivers, rooms and tours from different people.

We set out to change that: one team that meets you at the airport, settles you into your stay, opens the country's culture and history to you, and sees you off at the end. End to end, without the seams.

Destinations.title: Places that tell
Destinations.subtitle: A short guide to the sites we visit most, and why each one matters.

items.name: Kigali Genocide Memorial
items.summary: The final resting place of more than 250,000 victims of the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi.
items.context: Opened on the tenth commemoration, the memorial combines mass graves, gardens of reflection and an exhibition on how the genocide was planned, carried out and ended. It is the starting point for understanding modern Rwanda.
items.note: Allow at least two hours. Dress respectfully.

items.name: Kandt House Museum
items.summary: The home of Richard Kandt, the German explorer whose administrative post grew into Kigali.
items.context: Kandt was the first colonial Resident of Rwanda and settled here in 1907, which is why the city dates its founding to that year. The house is now a natural history museum with sweeping views over the city centre.
items.note: A short visit, easy to pair with a city-centre tour.

items.name: Rwanda Art Museum
items.summary: The former presidential palace, now home to contemporary Rwandan and African art.
items.context: This was the residence of President Juvénal Habyarimana. The wreckage of his plane, shot down on 6 April 1994, still lies in the grounds: the attack that preceded the genocide. Today the house hosts the national art collection.
items.note: Close to the airport, ideal on arrival or departure day.

items.name: Nyamata Church Memorial
items.summary: A church where thousands who sought refuge were killed, preserved as it was found.
items.context: Around 10,000 people were killed in and around the church in April 1994. The clothing of the victims still lies on the pews, making it one of the most direct and moving memorials in the country.
items.note: About 30 km south of Kigali. A heavy visit; plan a quiet afternoon after.

items.name: Campaign Against Genocide Museum
items.summary: Inside Parliament, the story of how the genocide was stopped.
items.context: Under the Arusha peace accords, a battalion of 600 RPF soldiers was stationed in this building. The museum follows their campaign from here in 1994, with the bullet-marked walls left as evidence.
items.note: Pairs well with the Kigali Genocide Memorial on the same day.

TripAlerts.title: Operational
TripAlerts.subtitle: Live updates regarding routes, border protocols, and fleet operations across the SURA network.
TripAlerts.reviewedNote: Border and health rules can change at short notice. Check with the Rwandan authorities or your embassy before you travel, and tell us if your plans involve a border crossing.

alerts.title: Ebola in the DRC: entry rules and border screening
alerts.content:
An Ebola (Bundibugyo) outbreak was declared in Ituri Province, DRC, on 15 May 2026, and the World Health Organization declared it a public health emergency of international concern on 17 May. Cases have also been reported in Uganda. There are no cases in Rwanda: tours, events and transfers inside the country run as normal.

What Rwanda requires (Ministry of Health, 22 May 2026):
• Foreign nationals who have been in, or transited through, the DRC in the 30 days before arrival are refused entry.
• Rwandan citizens and residents returning from the DRC go into quarantine.
• Everyone arriving is health-screened at Kigali International Airport and at the land border posts with the DRC.

The Rubavu–Goma crossings closed on 17 May and reopened in early July 2026 with screening in place. They can close again at short notice.

What this means for your trip:
• SURA does not run transfers into the DRC (Goma, Bukavu). Foreign visitors who cross into the DRC cannot re-enter Rwanda for 30 days.
• If you have been in the DRC recently, tell us before you book so we can plan around the 30-day rule.
• Rwanda Biomedical Centre health hotline: 114.

alerts.title: Travel close to the DRC border
alerts.content:
Fighting in eastern DRC can affect areas on the Rwandan side of the border, and several governments advise caution:
• The UK advises against all but essential travel to Rusizi District within 10 km of the DRC border, including Kamembe Airport and the Rwandan islands in Lake Kivu.
• The US advises against travel within 10 km of the DRC border. Volcanoes National Park is not included in that area.

Rubavu (Lake Kivu) and Rusizi are on our routes. We check conditions before each departure and will contact you if a route has to change. Please read your own government's travel advice and check that your travel insurance covers these areas.

alerts.title: New distance-based pricing with live fuel prices
alerts.content:
Our prices now follow the distance you actually travel and today's pump price of fuel, instead of flat daily rates.

• Fuel is charged per kilometre at each vehicle's own fuel price: petrol {petrol} RWF per litre (Standard sedans, Executive SUVs, Luxury SUVs) and diesel {diesel} RWF per litre (Premium SUVs, vans and coaches). Electric vehicles have no fuel charge.
• One-way trips with a driver include the driver's drive back. One-way self-drive trips include a vehicle collection fee instead.
• Airport transfers and city cab fares stay fixed, with the driver and fuel included.
• Every quote on our website shows the full price before you book, with a note on what it includes.

We update fuel prices whenever RURA announces a change.

alerts.title: Rwanda–Burundi land border remains closed
alerts.content: Burundi closed all land crossings with Rwanda on 11 January 2024, and they remain closed. SURA cannot run road transfers to or from Burundi. Flights between the two countries continue; travellers who must go by road can route through Tanzania.

alerts.title: Entry requirements for Rwanda
alerts.content:
• Visas: every nationality can get a visa on arrival, or apply online in advance through Irembo. Citizens of African Union, Commonwealth and Francophonie countries get a free 30-day visa. For most other nationalities a single-entry visa costs up to USD 50.
• Passport: valid for at least 6 months after you arrive, with a blank page for stamps.
• Yellow fever: carry your vaccination certificate if you arrive from a country with a risk of yellow fever.
• Health screening: expect screening on arrival (see the Ebola alert above).

sources.label: Rwanda Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration

alerts.title: Umuganda and car-free mornings
alerts.content:
• Umuganda (community work): on the last Saturday of each month, most services and traffic stop from 7:00 to 11:00.
• Car-free days in Kigali: on the first and third Sunday of each month, some roads are closed to cars from 7:00 to 10:00.

If your pickup falls in these hours, we will agree the timing with you in advance.

sources.label: UK travel advice: safety and security

alerts.title: Plastic bags and vapes are not allowed into Rwanda
alerts.content: Rwanda enforces a strict nationwide ban on non-biodegradable plastic bags: please make sure your luggage has none before you arrive, as they are confiscated at the border. Vapes and e-cigarettes are also illegal to bring in, even for personal use; they are confiscated and fines apply. SURA Essence provides eco-friendly refreshment packaging in all our vehicles.

alerts.title: Kigali Airport VIP Meet-and-Greet Processing Times
alerts.content: Due to increased seasonal volume, please allow up to 45 minutes for customs clearance upon arrival at KGL. Your SURA Driver will actively monitor your flight status and will wait at the arrivals terminal holding a standardized SURA identification board. No wait-time fees will be incurred for customs delays.

alerts.title: Luggage space by vehicle class
alerts.content: When you book a Standard sedan, luggage space is limited to 2 standard check-in bags. If you travel with heavy expedition gear, photography equipment or extra baggage, please book an Executive or Premium SUV, or a van for groups, for your comfort and safety.

alerts.title: Entry requirements for national parks
alerts.content: All clients embarking on Gorilla Trekking (Volcanoes National Park) or Safaris (Akagera) must ensure their permits are processed at least 72 hours prior to departure. SURA Essence concierge services can handle these logistics on your behalf. Ensure you carry your original passport for all internal transit.

intro.title: Kigali Outdoors
intro.headline: Beyond the hills
desc: Fresh air and open views, minutes from the city.
From a zipline on Mount Kigali to a slow round of golf.

venues.title: Fazenda Sengha
venues.summary: An outdoor activity park on the slopes of Mount Kigali.
history: Mount Kigali rises over the south-west of the city. Fazenda Sengha turned part of its slope into a recreation park, a short drive from the centre but well away from the traffic.
venues.visitorNote: Wear closed shoes. Activities are booked and paid on site.

venues.title: Kigali Golf Resort
venues.summary: An 18-hole course and tennis club in the Nyarutarama hills.
history: Now a full 18-hole course, the resort sits in one of Kigali's greenest neighbourhoods, with villas, a clubhouse and views across the valley.
venues.visitorNote: Tee times fill early at weekends. We can reserve one for you.

venues.title: Mamba Club
venues.summary: Bowling, volleyball and a relaxed garden bar.
history: A long-standing local favourite in Kimihurura, Mamba Club is where Kigali residents meet after work for a game and a drink.
venues.visitorNote: Lanes can be busy on Thursday and Friday evenings.

intro.title: Remembrance
intro.headline: Memorials and museums
desc: Rwanda's recent history, told with care.
Memorials are places of mourning; museums are places of learning. We prepare you for both.

venues.title: Kigali Genocide Memorial
venues.summary: The resting place of more than 250,000 victims of the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi.
history: The memorial opened in 2004, on the tenth commemoration of the genocide. It is built around mass graves, where victims from across Kigali are laid to rest.
Its exhibitions explain how the genocide was prepared and carried out, how it was stopped, and how Rwandans have worked towards justice and reconciliation since.
venues.visitorNote: Allow at least two hours. Some exhibits are distressing; we recommend it for visitors aged 12 and over.

venues.title: Kandt House Museum
venues.summary: The 1907 home of Richard Kandt, now a natural history museum.
history: Richard Kandt was a German explorer and the first colonial Resident of Rwanda. The administrative post he set up here in 1907 grew into the city of Kigali.
His house is one of the oldest buildings in the city. It now presents Rwanda's geology, plants and wildlife, with wide views over the city centre.
venues.visitorNote: A short visit that pairs easily with a city-centre tour.

venues.title: Nyamata Church Memorial
venues.summary: A church where thousands who sought refuge were killed in April 1994.
history: In April 1994, around 10,000 people who had gathered in and around Nyamata Catholic Church for safety were killed there.
The church has been kept as it was found. The clothing of the victims lies on the pews, and tens of thousands of victims from the surrounding area are buried in the crypts behind it.
venues.visitorNote: About 30 km south of Kigali. This is a very difficult visit; we recommend it for visitors aged 16 and over and suggest a quiet afternoon afterwards.

intro.title: Urban Pulse
intro.headline: Markets, art and neighbourhoods
desc: Everyday life in Kigali, up close.
Busy market halls, working studios and a neighbourhood that welcomes visitors.

venues.title: Kimironko Market
venues.summary: Kigali's busiest covered market for produce, fabric and tailoring.
history: Kimironko is where much of the city does its shopping. Beyond the fruit and vegetable stalls, its fabric section is known for bright kitenge prints, and tailors can make an outfit to measure within a day or two.
venues.visitorNote: Go in the morning. Prices are negotiable; our driver can help.

venues.title: Inema Arts Center
venues.summary: A contemporary art centre and working studios.
history: Founded by Rwandan artists, Inema shows contemporary painting and sculpture and gives local artists space to work, so visitors often meet the people behind the pieces.
venues.visitorNote: Works are for sale and can be packed for travel.

venues.title: Nyamirambo Walk
venues.summary: A guided walk through one of Kigali's oldest and liveliest neighbourhoods.
history: Nyamirambo grew up in colonial times and is home to Kigali's oldest mosque and a large Muslim community. Its streets of tailors, salons and small shops make it the city's most walkable district.
venues.visitorNote: Dress modestly. The walk can end with a home-cooked Rwandan lunch.

intro.title: Turning Points
intro.headline: The history that shaped modern Rwanda
desc: How the genocide was stopped, and what came after.
Museums and viewpoints that explain the country Rwanda has become.

venues.title: Campaign Against Genocide Museum
venues.summary: Inside Parliament, the story of how the genocide was stopped.
history: Under the Arusha peace accords, a battalion of 600 RPF soldiers was stationed in this building, then the national assembly. When the genocide began in April 1994, they left it to rescue civilians and fight to end the killing.
The museum opened in 2017. Its maps and displays follow that campaign, and the shell-marked walls of the building have been left as they were.
venues.visitorNote: Bring ID: the museum is inside the Parliament grounds.

venues.title: Rwanda Art Museum
venues.summary: The former presidential palace, now home to the national art collection.
history: This was the residence of President Juvénal Habyarimana. On 6 April 1994 his plane was shot down on its approach to Kigali, and the wreckage fell into the grounds. The genocide against the Tutsi began within hours.
Since 2018 the house has been the Rwanda Art Museum, showing contemporary Rwandan and African art. Remains of the aircraft can still be seen in the grounds.
venues.visitorNote: Close to the airport, so it fits well on your arrival or departure day.
highlights: The aircraft remains in the grounds

facts.driveTime: 30 min from the city centre, near the airport

venues.title: Rebero Hill
venues.summary: The best panoramic view of Kigali, from its southern hills.
history: Rebero overlooks the whole city from the south. The hill is also home to a national genocide memorial, a quiet place to pause before or after taking in the view.
venues.visitorNote: Go about an hour before sunset and bring a light jacket.
